B17C001.summary: After hearing of the slaughter of the Vrishnis and Krishna's ascent to heaven, Yudhishthira decides to give up the world, and his brothers agree. He hands the kingdom to Yuyutsu, places Parikshit on the throne under Kripa's teaching, and makes offerings for the dead. The Pandavas, Draupadi and a dog then set out eastward, and the fire god makes Arjuna give up his bow Gandiva before they head west and north to circle the earth.

scenes.B17C001S01: Janamejaya asks what the Pandavas did after the Vrishni disaster, and Yudhishthira resolves to renounce the world. He settles the kingdom and makes offerings and gifts before leaving.
scenes.B17C001S02: The citizens object, the Pandavas strip off their finery and fire rites, and the party sets out with a dog. At the sea, the fire god asks Arjuna to surrender Gandiva, and the travellers then turn north after circling the western coast.

shots.B17C001S01H01: Opening invocation that bows to Narayana, Nara and Sarasvati.
shots.B17C001S01H02: Janamejaya asks what the Pandavas did after hearing of the Vrishni and Andhaka fight and Krishna's ascent.
shots.B17C001S01H03: Vaishampayana reports that Yudhishthira, blaming Time, resolves to leave the world, and Arjuna and the twins agree.
shots.B17C001S01H04: The brothers hand the kingdom to Yuyutsu and install Parikshit, and Yudhishthira speaks to Subhadra about the rule of Parikshit and Vajra.
shots.B17C001S01H05: Yudhishthira offers water to the dead Yadavas and Krishna, honours sages with feasts and gifts, and places Parikshit under Kripa as his teacher.
shots.B17C001S02H01: Yudhishthira tells his subjects of his plan; they object but he persuades them. The brothers, Draupadi and the sacred fires are given up, and all put on bark garments.
shots.B17C001S02H02: The five brothers, Draupadi and a dog set out eastward while the citizens turn back, and Ulupi and Chitrangada go to their own places.
shots.B17C001S02H03: At the sea of red waters, the fire god appears and asks Arjuna to give up Gandiva and the quivers, and tells him the discus has vanished.
shots.B17C001S02H04: Arjuna throws the bow and quivers into the sea, the fire god departs, and the Pandavas turn south, west and north on their circuit of the earth.

B17C002.summary: The Pandavas climb north toward the Himalayas and Meru, and one by one they fall. Draupadi falls first, then Sahadeva, Nakula, Arjuna and Bhima, and Bhima asks Yudhishthira the cause of each fall. Yudhishthira names a fault in each, and he walks on alone with the dog, never looking back.

scenes.B17C002S01: On the northward journey Draupadi falls, followed by Sahadeva and Nakula. Yudhishthira explains each fall by a fault, and Bhima keeps asking why.
scenes.B17C002S02: Arjuna then falls, and Yudhishthira blames his boasting. Bhima falls next and begins to ask why, and the king walks on.
scenes.B17C002S03: Bhima, still lying on the ground, asks the king why he has fallen. Yudhishthira says it is his greed and boasting, and he walks on with only the dog.

shots.B17C002S01H01: The Pandavas cross Himavat and a sand desert and reach Meru; Draupadi falls, and Bhima asks Yudhishthira what she did wrong.
shots.B17C002S01H02: Yudhishthira says Draupadi favoured Arjuna above the others, and that she now bears the result.
shots.B17C002S01H03: Sahadeva falls, and Bhima asks why this humble brother has fallen.
shots.B17C002S01H04: Yudhishthira says Sahadeva thought no one equal to him in wisdom, and that this was his fault.
shots.B17C002S01H05: Nakula falls, and Bhima laments that this obedient brother, unmatched in beauty, has fallen too.
shots.B17C002S02H01: Yudhishthira says Nakula thought himself the most beautiful and that fate must be borne.
shots.B17C002S02H02: Arjuna falls in grief, and Bhima says Arjuna never spoke an untruth, so asks what evil brought him down.
shots.B17C002S02H03: Yudhishthira says Arjuna boasted he would defeat all foes in a single day and did not do it.
shots.B17C002S02H04: Yudhishthira walks on, and then Bhima falls.
shots.B17C002S02H05: Bhima, having fallen, begins to speak to Yudhishthira, calling himself the king's darling.
shots.B17C002S03H01: Bhima continues, asking the king why he has dropped down.
shots.B17C002S03H02: He asks the king to tell him the reason if he knows it.
shots.B17C002S03H03: Yudhishthira says Bhima ate greedily, boasted of strength, and never thought of others while eating.
shots.B17C002S03H04: Yudhishthira walks on without looking back, and only the dog follows him.

B17C003.summary: Shakra arrives with a chariot and invites Yudhishthira to heaven, but he refuses to go without his brothers and Draupadi. When Shakra insists he abandon the dog that has followed him, Yudhishthira refuses, arguing that abandoning one devoted to him is as sinful as killing a Brahmana. The dog then reveals itself as Dharma, who praises him, and Yudhishthira goes to heaven, where he insists on joining his brothers and Draupadi, closing the Mahaprasthanika section.

scenes.B17C003S01: Shakra invites Yudhishthira to his chariot, and Yudhishthira refuses to go without his brothers and asks that the dog be allowed to come.
scenes.B17C003S02: Shakra argues that dogs bar a man from heaven, and Yudhishthira refuses to abandon a devoted follower. The dog is revealed as Dharma, who praises Yudhishthira and recalls his earlier test at Dwaita.
scenes.B17C003S03: The gods carry Yudhishthira up to heaven, where Narada praises him. He declines to stay and says he will go wherever his brothers and Draupadi are.
scenes.B17C003S04: The title and author line of the Mahabharata, attributed to Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa.

shots.B17C003S01H01: Shakra arrives in a chariot, filling the sky and earth with noise, and invites the son of Pritha to climb aboard; Yudhishthira says he will not go without his brothers and Draupadi.
shots.B17C003S01H02: Shakra replies that the brothers have gone to heaven before him and that Yudhishthira alone will go there in his own body.
shots.B17C003S01H03: Yudhishthira asks that the dog, devoted to him, be allowed to come along.
shots.B17C003S01H04: Shakra offers immortality and heaven's rewards if Yudhishthira casts off the dog, which he says is not cruel.
shots.B17C003S01H05: Yudhishthira refuses, saying it is hard for a righteous man to commit an unrighteous act, and he will not give up one devoted to him.
shots.B17C003S02H01: Shakra says there is no place in heaven for those with dogs, and that the Krodhavasas take away their merit, so he should abandon the dog.
shots.B17C003S02H02: Yudhishthira says abandoning a devoted follower is as sinful as killing a Brahmana, and lists the people he vows never to forsake.
shots.B17C003S02H03: Shakra says a dog's sight of offerings takes them away, and Yudhishthira answers that he could not revive his dead brothers and lists four acts equal to abandoning a devoted one.
shots.B17C003S02H04: The dog changes into Dharma, the god of righteousness, who speaks to Yudhishthira with praise.
shots.B17C003S02H05: Dharma recalls the test at the Dwaita woods, where Yudhishthira asked for Nakula's revival, and says he gave up heaven's chariot rather than the dog, so his reward is secure.
shots.B17C003S03H01: Dharma, Shakra, the Maruts, the Ashvinis and others lift Yudhishthira onto a car to heaven, and Narada praises him as the only man to reach heaven in his own body.
shots.B17C003S03H02: Yudhishthira greets the gods and sages and says he will go wherever his brothers have gone, whether happy or miserable.
shots.B17C003S03H03: Shakra urges him to stay in the heaven he has earned and asks why human affections still hold him.
shots.B17C003S03H04: Yudhishthira says he will not stay apart from his brothers and Draupadi, and wants to go where they have gone.
shots.B17C003S03H05: A line marking the end of the Mahaprasthanika section.
